- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >35.0), model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply downward correction by 1–2% of spike magnitude.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.5) and price is trending down, model often underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% per negative sentiment day.
- Model frequently fails to capture late-stage rallies (last 5–7 days of 30d horizon); if sentiment turns positive mid-horizon, increase forecast slope toward end.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >36.0 and sentiment is neutral or negative, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0 to align with recent mean (~35.0–35.5).
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment was positive 3–5 days ago, model often underreacts; adjust forecast upward by 0.3–0.7 to reflect delayed momentum.
